repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
wait until((#Main_SoundSensor).soundSensor_sound <= 30 and (#Bedroom_SoundSensor).soundSensor_sound <= 30)
triggered = false
}
wait until((#Main_SoundSensor).soundSensor_sound > 30 or (#Bedroom_SoundSensor).soundSensor_sound > 30)
any(#AirPurifier).airPurifier_setAirPurifierMode("sleep")
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The candidate incorrectly requires both sensors to be in opposite states (Main > 30 AND Bedroom <= 30) before firing, whereas the IR requires a rising edge on SoundSensor (any/all) > 30. Additionally, the candidate uses `all(#AirPurifier)` which targets both devices, but the binding slot for AirPurifier is a plain list, implying a single target selection or that the IR expects a specific device context not fully resolved by `all`. The mismatch at 1000ms shows the IR did nothing (condition not met or edge not rising) while the candidate fired. The IR `cycle` with `wait(cond, rising)` must block until the predicate becomes true from false, then execute once per period.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the complex dual-sensor guard with a simple rising-edge wait on the union of sound sensors (> 30). Changed `all(#AirPurifier)` to `any(#AirPurifier)` to match the existential nature of the binding slot `any` for AirPurifier, ensuring only one device is targeted per cycle instance as implied by the binding structure. Preserved the 1 SEC period and the rising-edge logic.
